title: Are Large Language Models Chameleons? An Attempt to Simulate Social Surveys

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting large language models with specific gender identities (man/woman) and comparing the mean and distribution of their simulated survey responses against ground-truth human data from the European Social Survey.

Prompting models with specific birth years to simulate survey respondents and evaluating how well the model's generated responses match the actual age-distributed response patterns in the real survey data.

Prompting models with different European countries of residence (e.g., Germany, Greece, Bulgaria, Italy) and measuring geographic disparities in how accurately the model replicates regional public opinion and survey response distributions.

Injecting International Standard Classification of Occupations (ISCO) categories into user prompts to evaluate whether specifying occupational backgrounds improves or alters the variance and accuracy of LLM simulated survey responses.
